# Spec — MCP runtime harness for standalone Waica Projects
<!-- Generated by /skill:sdd-spec on 2026-08-07. Source: issue #24 + grill issue-24-run-and-observe-waica-projects-through--20260807-0860c473. Status: approved -->
<!-- SDD-Tracking: issue=#24; grill=issue-24-run-and-observe-waica-projects-through--20260807-0860c473 -->

## Context

The MCP currently reconstructs and validates a Project from files, but all ten tools stop at static state (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts:49-153`). A standalone Project creates its `Game` inside a local `main()` binding and starts it after scene load (`packages/editor/template/src/main.ts:79-104`), so an agent must patch Project source to inspect live entities, components or stats. The engine already owns those values (`packages/engine/src/game.ts:49-60`), but its frame loop is private and wall-clock-driven (`packages/engine/src/game.ts:172-230`), `Input` only consumes DOM keyboard events (`packages/engine/src/input.ts:13-27,89-97`), and MCP results currently contain JSON text only (`packages/mcp/src/server.ts:257-267`).

This spec deliberately supersedes `.sdd/specs/waica-mcp.md`'s prior run/bridge/screenshot non-goal. It implements the confirmed handoff and ADR-0005/ADR-0006: an engine-owned, session-scoped Runtime Bridge and deterministic-by-default Run Sessions, without editing Project source.

## Expected behavior

- **CA-1 — Runtime Bridge activation, lifecycle and compatibility (HIGH):** `@waica/engine` implements Runtime Bridge protocol version `1`. During ordinary execution, with no pre-page activation hook, `Game.start()`, `Game.stop()`, `Game.dispose()`, rendering, input and update behavior remain unchanged; no permanent string-named global or network control endpoint is exposed, and there is no per-frame bridge work. When an MCP browser context installs the ephemeral hook before navigation, `Game.start()` registers that fully constructed live game and reports protocol version, installed engine version and its Game surface; `dispose()` or page unload unregisters it. Exactly one live `Game` may be registered: zero prevents readiness, a second live instance fails the Run Session, and a replacement is accepted only after the old instance has unregistered. An engine without protocol `1` produces `runtime-incompatible` at stage `bridge` with the minimum compatible engine version; the MCP never patches or polyfills it.

- **CA-2 — Deterministic and real-time frame control (HIGH):** An activated Run Session reaches readiness after Project modules, persisted params, scene entities, component `onReady`, camera and UI have loaded, but before the first simulation frame: mode `paused`, frame `0`, simulation time `0`. This pause is distinct from the editor's existing `game.simulate = false`: while paused, component updates, collisions, camera stepping, `Game.onUpdate` callbacks and input end-of-frame advancement do not run, but the current Game surface and visible `GameUi` remain rendered. A manual step runs the same ordered frame pipeline as real time—resolved component updates, collisions, camera, `Game.onUpdate`, input end-frame, render—then increments frame and simulation time. `step` defaults to `dt = 1/60`, accepts only finite `0 < dt <= 0.1`, and advances 1–600 frames per call. `resume` enters RAF-driven `real-time`; `pause` returns to deterministic mode without applying wall-clock catch-up, and both are idempotent. Existing editor edit-mode semantics and ordinary non-MCP real-time behavior stay unchanged.

- **CA-3 — Semantic action injection (HIGH):** `control_runtime` injects only action names installed in the live `Input` bindings. `press` creates one held + just-pressed frame and automatically releases after that simulation frame; `hold` creates one just-pressed edge and remains held across frames until `release`; another `press`/`hold` while already down creates no second edge; `release` on an up action is harmless. Unknown actions fail with `runtime-operation-failed` at stage `control` and list available actions. While paused, injected state remains queued until the next manual step; in real-time it is observed by the next RAF frame. Existing `consume()`/`consumed()` semantics still guarantee one press can be spent only once. Physical key codes, pointer input and arbitrary DOM events are unavailable through the bridge.

- **CA-4 — Structured Runtime Snapshots (HIGH):** `inspect_runtime` returns shared runtime metadata plus a read-only `snapshot` with this stable shape:
  - `bridgeVersion: 1`, `mode: 'paused' | 'real-time'`, zero-based `frame`, accumulated `simulationTime`;
  - `stats`, a key-sorted object containing every current `Game.stats` entry;
  - `entities`, in live insertion order, each with an opaque string `id` stable and never reused within that live `Game`, `name`, and `transform` containing numeric `position {x,y,z}`, `rotation {x,y,z,order}` and `scale {x,y,z}`;
  - `components`, in entity component order, each with `type`, zero-based `index` and projected `state`;
  - `projectionIssues`, an ordered list of paths and projection markers generated by CA-5.

  Runtime-spawned entities appear and destroyed entities disappear; duplicate names remain distinguishable by id. Optional `entity_ids`, `entity_names` and `component_types` filters are OR within one category and AND across categories. A component filter removes nonmatching components and entities left with none. No match is a successful snapshot with `entities: []`; stats and temporal metadata remain. Entity/component order is preserved and projected record keys are lexicographically sorted. The tool exposes no arbitrary JavaScript evaluation or state mutation.

- **CA-5 — Bounded component-state projection (HIGH):** Without an override, a live component projects own enumerable fields whose names do not start with `_`, plus setter-backed accessors from its prototype chain. `entity`, `game` and functions are excluded; fields declared `static transient` are included because this is runtime inspection, not authoring defaults. Getter failures become error markers and never fail the whole snapshot. A component may replace discovery with `inspectState(): unknown`; its return value is still passed through the same safe projector, and a thrown error becomes a marker.

  The projector preserves `null`, booleans, strings and finite numbers; recursively handles arrays and plain records; represents `Date`, `BigInt`, `Map` and `Set` with explicit typed JSON objects; and emits objects with a `$waica` discriminator for `cycle`, `unsupported`, `error` or `truncated`. It never invokes arbitrary `toJSON()`. Limits are depth 5, 100 entries per array/record/Map/Set, 4 KiB per string, 64 KiB of serialized state per component and 1 MiB per snapshot. String truncation retains a preview and original length; collection/component/snapshot truncation records the omitted count or path. Reaching a limit truncates deterministically and adds `projectionIssues`; it does not fail the tool or silently coerce values. The engine root exports the inspection types and optional `Component.inspectState` contract.

- **CA-6 — Public MCP surface and result contracts (HIGH):** The server registers exactly 15 tools: the existing ten plus `start_project`, `stop_project`, `inspect_runtime`, `control_runtime` and `capture_screenshot`. Every new tool requires absolute `project_path`, resolves it to a canonical real path internally, rejects additional properties and exposes no session id.
  - `start_project`: optional `browser_executable_path`, `headless` (default `true`), `viewport {width,height}` and `timeout_ms` (default 30,000; integer 1,000–120,000).
  - `stop_project`: no fields beyond `project_path`.
  - `inspect_runtime`: optional arrays `entity_ids`, `entity_names`, `component_types`.
  - `control_runtime`: one `operation` from `press | hold | release | pause | resume | step`; action operations require `action`; `step` accepts `dt` and `frames`; incompatible fields are rejected.
  - `capture_screenshot`: no fields beyond `project_path`.

  `start_project` and `stop_project` are idempotent execution tools; `inspect_runtime` and `capture_screenshot` carry `readOnlyHint: true`; `control_runtime` is not read-only. Successful runtime tools return the canonical `projectPath`, URL when active, installed `engineVersion`, `bridgeVersion: 1`, current mode/frame/time and project-engine provenance `{package:'@waica/engine', version, source:'project'}` where applicable. `control_runtime` additionally returns sorted held actions and never embeds a snapshot. `capture_screenshot` returns one JSON metadata text block, the same metadata in `structuredContent`, and one `image/png` block; base64 image bytes are not duplicated in text or structured content.

  Runtime tool failures set MCP `isError: true` and use a stable error body with `code`, `stage`, `message`, canonical `projectPath` and optional `diagnostics`. Codes are `runtime-unsupported-host`, `runtime-prerequisite-missing`, `runtime-start-failed`, `runtime-incompatible`, `runtime-not-running`, `runtime-invalid-state` and `runtime-operation-failed`; stages are `project`, `package-manager`, `dependencies`, `dev-server`, `browser`, `page`, `bridge`, `game`, `control` and `cleanup`.

- **CA-7 — Startup preflight, Project command and browser selection (HIGH):** The MVP supports macOS and Linux. Windows rejects `start_project` before mutation with `runtime-unsupported-host`; every existing non-runtime MCP tool continues working there. Startup requires a valid Waica Project, a readable `package.json`, a nonempty `scripts.dev`, already resolvable Project dependencies and an available package-manager executable. It selects the manager from a valid root `packageManager` field, otherwise exactly one root lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`), otherwise npm; an unsupported field value or conflicting lockfiles is an actionable prerequisite error. It supports npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun but never runs install, mutates a lockfile or downloads a browser.

  The trusted Project's declared `dev` script is run from the canonical Project root with Vite-compatible `--host 127.0.0.1 --port <allocated-loopback-port> --strictPort`; no arbitrary command is accepted. The MCP chooses a currently free loopback port and retries a detected bind collision with a newly allocated port a bounded number of times. The emitted loopback URL is parsed and probed. A script that exits, binds non-loopback, fails to forward the required options or never reports a usable URL fails at `dev-server`. Browser selection uses the explicit path when supplied, otherwise deterministic macOS/Linux Chrome/Chromium discovery; compatibility means `playwright-core` can launch it and create the required isolated context. Viewport defaults to valid positive `src/game.json.resolution.width/height`, otherwise 640×360; explicit dimensions must be positive integers with at most 1,000,000 pixels, and browser device scale factor is 1.

  Readiness requires process alive + HTTP page loaded + bridge v1 + exactly one live `Game` + successful initial snapshot. Timeout or failure captures at most the final 64 KiB each of stdout/stderr and the final 100 browser console/page errors, reports the failed stage, and cleans every resource. A successful `start_project` returns `reused`, viewport, runtime metadata and `initialSnapshot`.

- **CA-8 — Run Session identity, concurrency, reload and cleanup (HIGH):** A Run Session is keyed by filesystem real path, so symlink aliases coalesce. Concurrent/repeated starts for one Project share one in-flight start and ultimately return the same session (`reused: false` to its creator, `true` thereafter) without duplicate process/browser resources. Different canonical Projects may start and run concurrently in isolated browser contexts. `stop_project` waits until browser context and whole dev-server process group are gone and the port is closed; when no session exists it succeeds with `{stopped:false}`, otherwise `{stopped:true}`. Cleanup sends graceful termination to the process group, waits two seconds, then force-kills survivors; failure to prove cleanup returns stage `cleanup` rather than claiming success.

  Full page reload/HMR may replace the old `Game` only after unload/unregistration. The session enters a transient reloading state, rejects other runtime operations with `runtime-invalid-state`, and waits the configured startup timeout for one new bridge/game; success resets it to paused frame/time zero, while timeout, page/browser/dev-process failure, a second simultaneous `Game`, or MCP transport closure ends the session and cleans all owned resources. Sessions are never persisted or reattached. The server close path cleans all concurrent sessions before completing.

- **CA-9 — Real browser readiness and control (MEDIUM):** Against a real temporary Vite Waica Project and host-installed Chromium/Chrome, `start_project` starts the declared script, reports the actual loopback URL only after a paused initial snapshot is available, and leaves Project source byte-identical. A fixture whose HTTP page responds but throws before `Game.start()` must fail at `page` or `bridge`, proving HTTP 200 alone is not readiness. The live fixture can receive `hold('right')`, step an exact number of frames, release, and expose the expected entity/component/state and frame/time changes through `inspect_runtime`. A real page reload returns to a fresh paused baseline or fails/cleans according to CA-8.

- **CA-10 — Game-surface screenshots (MEDIUM):** `capture_screenshot` works in paused and real-time modes and captures the Game host containing both the WebGL canvas and Waica HTML UI, never browser chrome or unrelated full-page content. The PNG has the actual Game-surface dimensions at DPR 1, fits the 1,000,000-pixel viewport cap and the MCP stdio message limit, and is correlated to the current bridge version, mode, frame and simulation time. A real fixture with a known contrasting HTML UI overlay proves by decoding the returned PNG in Chromium and sampling its pixel that UI is included. PNG signature/dimensions, metadata equality and absence of duplicated base64 are machine-asserted. Pausing a Run Session must not hide that UI.

- **CA-11 — Dependency, build and published-artifact shape (HIGH):** `playwright-core` is the sole new browser automation runtime dependency and has the same range in private `@waica/mcp` and published `@waica/cli`; no Playwright/Puppeteer browser package or browser binary is bundled. CLI/MCP package tests update their exact dependency assertions. The CLI still vendors the built MCP and the three `@waica` libraries, while normal package installation supplies `playwright-core` and its transitive dependencies. A fresh build contains all runtime-harness modules with explicit ESM extensions, and the symlink-free packed sandbox can launch the bundled MCP and resolve `playwright-core`. All package versions remain unchanged and lockstep; this work does not publish.

- **CA-12 — Blocking checkout and packed-CLI browser gates (MEDIUM):** Root `pnpm test:e2e` runs a network-free generated/controlled fixture through the built checkout CLI and real stdio: start, readiness, initial snapshot, action input, deterministic step, changed snapshot, PNG, explicit stop, closed port and no child process. It also includes the HTTP-200-without-Game negative readiness case. `pnpm test:dist` invokes the same critical happy path against the packed CLI inside its existing materialized sandbox after package-shape checks. Both commands fail—not skip—when compatible Chrome is absent, and always clean temporary Projects, MCP, browser and dev processes on assertion failure. Browser failure matrices that are cheaper to model (package managers, timeout stages, concurrency, kill escalation, projection edges) remain deterministic unit/integration tests rather than duplicated browser cases.

- **CA-13 — Documentation and autonomy contract (LOW):** MCP/CLI READMEs list and describe all 15 tools, state that `start_project` executes trusted Project code without a sandbox, document installed dependencies and system Chrome as prerequisites, explain macOS/Linux scope and Windows rejection, describe deterministic pause/control/snapshot/screenshot semantics, and state that stop/MCP close owns cleanup. `.sdd/specs/waica-mcp.md` marks its old run/bridge/screenshot exclusion superseded by issue #24 instead of leaving contradictory guidance. `.sdd/project.md` records `pnpm test:e2e`, the Chrome prerequisite, its real observed duration/result, and the new browser rung while preserving subjective game feel as human-only. `CONTEXT.md` and ADR-0005/0006 remain consistent with the shipped contract.

## Out of scope

- Editor Play integration or editor file watching.
- Windows runtime sessions in the MVP; existing static/scaffold MCP tools still support Windows.
- Attaching to an externally owned browser, persistent/recoverable sessions, or a network control endpoint.
- Multiple simultaneous live `Game` instances in one Project page or public session/game ids.
- Patching Project source, transforming Vite modules, or polyfilling older engines.
- Installing Project dependencies, changing lockfiles, downloading a browser, or accepting arbitrary shell commands.
- Arbitrary in-page JavaScript evaluation or mutation of live entities/components/stats.
- Physical keyboard codes, pointer/gamepad/touch input or arbitrary DOM events.
- Full-page/canvas-only screenshot modes, video recording or visual-diff baselines.
- Automated judgment of game feel, animation quality or visual correctness.
- Package version bumps, npm publishing, release tags or merging a PR.

## Verifiability

**Mixed:** CA-1 through CA-8 and CA-11 are **HIGH** because their bridge, frame, input, serializer, schema, package-selection and session-state behavior can be expressed as deterministic Vitest unit/integration tests under the contract's verified `pnpm test`, with type/build/package-shape support. CA-9, CA-10 and CA-12 are **MEDIUM** because they require a real Vite process and system Chromium; the contract currently has only semi-automated browser driving and explicitly records the absence of a scripted e2e suite. CA-13 is **LOW** because grep and file assertions prove documentation presence, not truth. No criterion is NULL: subjective game feel and visual judgment are explicitly out of scope rather than hidden as human acceptance.

The repository has no active generation policy for PR size, coverage, dependencies or commits. The cross-package blast radius and new `playwright-core` dependency therefore do not violate a gate, but this remains a large implementation. No size policy authorizes dropping any of the four capabilities confirmed by the grill. The browser gate introduced here must refresh `.sdd/project.md`; until implementation proves `pnpm test:e2e`, the MEDIUM grade must not be inflated.

## Verification plan

The user selected layered TDD plus two focused real-browser gates: deterministic tests own every rule and failure branch; browser tests prove only the integration claims mocks cannot observe.

| CA | Verification mechanism |
|---|---|
| CA-1 | New engine bridge tests under `pnpm test`: no-hook characterization; activation before page; v1 handshake; register/unregister; zero/one/two/replacement Game matrix; no public endpoint. Existing `game.test.ts` remains green. |
| CA-2 | Mocked renderer/RAF tests assert frame-zero readiness, no paused callbacks/input clearing, visible UI, exact manual/realtime pipeline order, dt/frame bounds, pause/resume no catch-up, and unchanged `simulate=false`. |
| CA-3 | Extend `input.test.ts` plus state-machine integration: press/hold/release matrix, repeated-down edge suppression, consume semantics, paused queue and real-time-next-frame behavior. |
| CA-4 | Pure/in-memory snapshot fixtures: spawned/destroyed/duplicate-name entities, stable ids, stats, transforms, components, filters, no-match, ordering and temporal metadata deepEqual. |
| CA-5 | Pure projector matrix: own/accessor/transient/backref/private-prefix fields; primitives, non-finite numbers, Date/BigInt/Map/Set, cycles, getters/overrides that throw, every exact limit and deterministic top-level truncation. |
| CA-6 | Extend `server.test.ts` over `InMemoryTransport`: exact 15-tool set, schemas/annotations, conditional control arguments, canonical paths, all success/error shapes, screenshot text + structured metadata + image block with no duplicated bytes. |
| CA-7 | `mkdtemp` Project matrix with injected spawn/browser adapters: host support, manager precedence/conflicts, missing script/deps/binary/browser, exact command/cwd/flags, explicit/discovered Chrome, viewport/timeout validation, HTTP-not-ready and bounded diagnostics. |
| CA-8 | Session-manager integration tests with controllable child/browser fakes and real short-lived child-process fixtures: symlink aliases, simultaneous starts, parallel Projects, stop idempotency, reload transition, crashes, TERM→force escalation, MCP close and port/process cleanup. |
| CA-9 | `pnpm test:e2e`: real Vite Project and Chrome prove source bytes unchanged, bridge-backed readiness, initial frame zero, semantic input + exact steps + changed snapshot, and HTTP-200-without-Game rejection. |
| CA-10 | Same e2e returns PNG; assert signature/IHDR dimensions/metadata/no base64 duplication, then load it back into Chromium and sample the fixture's known HTML overlay pixel. Capture once paused and once real-time. |
| CA-11 | Package unit tests + `pnpm build` + package-shape leg of `pnpm test:dist`: exact mirrored `playwright-core`, no browser package/binary, clean ESM dist, packed resolution and unchanged lockstep versions. |
| CA-12 | Checkout `pnpm test:e2e` and packed-CLI continuation inside `pnpm test:dist`; both assert explicit stop, closed URL/port, no child process and cleanup in `finally`. Missing Chrome is a red failure, never a skip. |
| CA-13 | Grep/deep file assertions for all 15 tool names, trust/Chrome/host/cleanup docs, supersession text, ADR/glossary terms and a refreshed `.sdd/project.md` row with the command's measured result. |

Red-green-refactor uses focused Vitest files first, then the browser fixture after the deterministic layers are green. Final local ladder before PR:

```bash
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
pnpm test:e2e
pnpm test:dist
```

The final report must state the discovered Chrome executable/version and exact duration/results for both browser gates. It must not claim subjective game feel or visual correctness was verified.

## Execution changelog

- **2026-08-08 — [DEVIATION, confirmed]:** Vite 8.1.5 treats CLI `--port 0` as falsy and binds its default 5173 (`vite --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0 --strictPort` was observed returning `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`). That made CA-7's literal mechanism incompatible with CA-8's concurrent Projects. The user confirmed replacing it with an MCP-allocated free loopback port plus bounded bind-collision retry. Scope and externally observable behavior are unchanged; only the impossible port-selection mechanism changed.

## Risks and gaps

- **Browser e2e is a new harness, not an existing contract capability.** Until the implementation runs and `.sdd/project.md` is refreshed, CA-9/10/12 remain MEDIUM. The current machine has system Google Chrome, but Linux publish-host availability must be exercised rather than assumed.
- **Windows is deliberately excluded from Run Sessions.** Other MCP tools continue to work; adding Windows later requires process-tree cleanup, executable discovery and a real Windows gate.
- **`playwright-core` changes the published CLI dependency graph.** The private MCP cannot rely on a dependency absent from `@waica/cli`; package tests and the packed sandbox must catch drift.
- **MCP stdio defaults to a 10 MiB message buffer.** The 1,000,000-pixel/DPR-1 viewport and snapshot limits are contract safeguards; the run must prove worst-case tool responses remain below the transport limit.
- **Process cleanup is OS-sensitive.** Descendants that deliberately detach can escape ordinary group signaling. The spec requires proof for the process tree the tool starts and an honest cleanup error if it cannot prove termination; it does not promise an OS sandbox.
- **Project code is trusted and executes twice in different contexts today:** `validate_project` may execute modules in the MCP process, while a Run Session executes the full Project in its dev process/browser. Issue #27's validation subprocess remains separate and is not a prerequisite.
- **Runtime projection may expose Project-owned state.** It is local and read-only, but limits and `inspectState()` must be documented; arbitrary evaluation/mutation remains forbidden.
- **Getter/override code can have side effects or throw.** Errors become markers, but a trusted component author controls that code. The default projector does not call arbitrary `toJSON()`.
- **HMR can create registration races.** The zero/one/two Game state machine and timeout cleanup must be attacked in unit tests; the browser gate covers one real reload only.
- **Paused UI conflicts with current `simulate=false`.** Reusing that flag would violate CA-2/10 because it hides UI and still advances host callbacks/input framing.
- **The platformer example is not the browser fixture.** Open issue #31 currently prevents it from booting; the e2e uses a controlled generated fixture so #31 does not block this spec.
- **No CI runs on PRs.** All five final commands are local pre-PR gates; publish CI later re-runs `test:dist` on Linux.
- No package version bump, npm publish, release tag or human game-feel check is part of execution.
